activities.title: True or false: STARs and frequencies
activities.intro: Decide if each statement is true or false.

cards.s: Published speed restrictions on a STAR are mandatory unless ATC modifies them.
An MEA printed on a STAR is a crossing restriction you must meet at the fix.
cards.why: False. MEAs are not restrictions, but stay above them unless ATC clears you lower [[33:394|AIM 5-4-1a2]].

cards.s: A pilot who does not want STARs can write "NO STAR" in the flight plan remarks.
Controllers may leave the departure frequency out of a clearance when it is printed on an assigned DP.
Center sector frequencies appear only in the Chart Supplement, not on en route charts.
cards.why: False. En route charts show Centers and sector frequencies [[29:66|IPH 2-6]] [[2:67|Chart Users' Guide p 67]].

cards.s: Under "descend via", the pilot reports the altitude leaving and the procedure name on each new frequency.
cards.why: True, plus the runway transition if assigned and any unpublished restrictions [[33:395|AIM 5-4-1a2]].

cards.s: If a Center frequency goes quiet, call Flight Service right away.
cards.why: False. Wait at least 1 minute, then try the transferring controller or another Center frequency before Flight Service [[29:108|IPH 2-48]].

Review the DP and note its departure frequency
Tune frequencies, set up navigation equipment, call ground and taxi

On the runway: heading indicator and compass agree, transponder ALT, lights and pitot heat on

activities.title: Work the numbers you will teach
activities.intro: Work it out, then type your answer.

items.q: Your learner is inbound on the 160° radial and must intercept the 205° radial inbound. Using the IFH method, what intercept angle does he use?
Same problem: to what heading does he turn to intercept?
ADF: to intercept the 355° inbound bearing, he turns to 355° and the needle points 40° right. Doubling the relative bearing, what interception heading does he fly?
Two VORs are 72 NM apart on a straight airway segment with no changeover point charted. How far from the first VOR does he change frequencies?
items.why: With no COP charted on a straight segment, change midway: 72 ÷ 2 = 36 NM [[23:29|IFH 1-10]] [[33:381|AIM 5-3-6]].

items.q: At HAYED at 12,000 ft he must cross PENNS at 6,000. Planned descent 500 fpm, groundspeed 180 knots. At least how far before PENNS does he start down?
items.why: 6,000 ÷ 500 = 12 minutes; at 3 NM per minute, 12 × 3 = 36 NM [[29:132|IPH Figure 3-17]].

items.q: Using the IPH rule of thumb, how many NM out should he start down to lose 6,000 ft?
What rate of descent gives a 3° path at 120 knots groundspeed?
The IPH rate of climb table example: a SID requires 297 ft per NM and the groundspeed is 180 knots. What rate of climb does that take, in fpm?
items.why: 180 knots is 3 NM a minute, so 297 × 3 ≈ 891; the TPP rate of climb table in the IPH example gives 892 fpm [[29:34|IPH Figure 1-17]]. If the airplane cannot make it, he should not accept the SID [[29:45|IPH 1-29]].

activities.title: An IFR lesson from the right seat
activities.intro: You are the CFII on a training flight in IMC with an instrument learner. Make each teaching call as the flight unfolds.

steps.s: Briefing. The planned SID has a climb gradient above standard. Your learner says the airplane "probably" makes it.
options: Accept the SID and watch the VSI on the climb
File it anyway; ATC will vector him if he falls short
Have him convert the gradient to fpm for his groundspeed and refuse the SID if unable
Ignore the gradient, since it is meant for jets
steps.why: If he cannot meet a SID's climb gradient he should not accept it, even if ATC assigns it [[29:45|IPH 1-29]]; the TPP rate of climb table relates gradients and groundspeeds [[29:34|IPH 1-18]].

steps.s: Climbing on the SID, departure says, "Turn left heading 270, maintain 4,000." The SID had a crossing restriction at 5,000 ahead.
options: Fly 270 and 4,000; the SID is canceled unless told to expect to resume
Keep the SID's restrictions and climb to 5,000
Fly 270 but keep climbing via the SID
Refuse the vector until the SID is complete
steps.why: Vectored off a SID, consider it canceled with its altitude and speed restrictions unless ATC says "expect to resume SID" [[33:355|AIM 5-2-9h3]], and comply promptly with assigned headings and altitudes [[34:5|AIM 5-5-6]].

steps.s: En route he flies the airway on the magenta line, but he has not identified the VOR tuned on NAV 1 as his backup.
options: Leave it; the GPS is primary
Turn the VOR off to reduce clutter
Pull the GPS breaker as a surprise test
Have him identify the VOR now and brief why
steps.why: Listen to the identifier before relying on a VOR [[23:254|IFH 9-11]]; using VOR to back up GPS is one of the PHAK's ways to keep situational awareness [[1:70|PHAK 2-31]].

steps.s: ATC says, "Descend via the arrival." He starts down toward the STAR's lowest altitude without checking the "at or above" restriction at the next fix.
options: Praise the early descent
Stop him: descend at his discretion, but meet every published restriction
Tell him descend via means 500 fpm
Have him hold altitude until a new clearance
steps.why: "Descend via" lets him descend at his discretion, but he must meet all published altitude and speed restrictions [[33:393|AIM 5-4-1a2]].

steps.s: Debrief. He complied with every clearance, but you saw him heads-down at every change. What do you plan for the next lesson?
options: Repeat the same flight until it is perfect
Move on; compliance is all the PTS asks
Add a scenario where a clearance conflicts with terrain or performance, and let him decide
Fly without the MFD so he cannot rely on it
steps.why: Aim for correlation, not repetition [[25:66|AIH 3-15]]; a good scenario has no obvious single answer and builds decision-making [[25:120|AIH 5-17]].
